eyebrow: SQL for Oracle Financials · Chapter Two
subtitle: Lesson 6 · Joining Financial Tables

steps.label: FUSION TODAY
steps.sub: renamed POZ_SUPPLIERS, but VENDOR_ID stuck around

code:
SELECT s.vendor_name, i.invoice_num, i.invoice_amount
FROM poz_suppliers s
INNER JOIN ap_invoices_all i
    ON s.vendor_id = i.vendor_id;
caption: No AS before either alias — the rule from Lesson 2 applies to every join.

steps.label: MATCHED
steps.sub: supplier has at least one invoice — kept

eyebrow: WHERE still works after a JOIN
code:
SELECT s.vendor_name, i.invoice_num, i.invoice_amount
FROM poz_suppliers s
INNER JOIN ap_invoices_all i
    ON s.vendor_id = i.vendor_id
WHERE i.invoice_amount > 10000
ORDER BY i.invoice_amount DESC;
caption: WHERE filters the already-joined rows — now with columns from both tables to filter on.

subtitle: Connecting an invoice to what actually settled it.
